subtitle: Repository-owned full-pair integration falsifier

rows.recognition_route: Combine the horizontal forces into the net force on the selected object before applying Newton's second law.

questions.stem: A 2 kg block on a frictionless horizontal surface has a 6 N horizontal force to the right. What is its acceleration?

attempt.workspace: Identify the selected system, write the governing relation, then solve with direction and units.

hints.content: Notice that the given horizontal force is the net horizontal force on the selected block.
Use the Grade 9 Newton's-second-law model F_net = m a for the selected block.
Start from a = F_net / m, then substitute 6 N and 2 kg.

questions.stem: Two horizontal forces, 10 N right and 4 N left, act on a 2 kg object. Determine the acceleration and direction.

attempt.workspace: Identify the governing model without a concept cue. Resolve direction before calculating acceleration.

hints.content: The two horizontal forces oppose each other, so direction matters before magnitudes are combined.
Find the net force on the selected object, then apply F_net = m a.

repair.target: Re-read the solution's force-direction and model-selection steps.

solutions.recap: The selected block has mass 2 kg and a net horizontal force of 6 N to the right.
solutions.why: Newton's second law connects the net force on the selected system to its mass and acceleration.
solutions.method: Use F_net = m a. Rearrange to a = F_net / m and substitute 6 N / 2 kg = 3 m/s^2.
solutions.answer_check: The acceleration is 3 m/s^2 to the right. Its direction matches the net force, and the units reduce to m/s^2.
solutions.concept_to_keep: Fix the selected system and the net force before substituting into Newton's second law.

solutions.recap: The selected object has 10 N to the right and 4 N to the left, with mass 2 kg.
solutions.why: The opposing forces must first be combined as directed quantities; Newton's second law then uses that net force.
solutions.method: Take right as positive. The net force is 10 N - 4 N = 6 N to the right. Then a = F_net / m = 6 N / 2 kg = 3 m/s^2.
solutions.answer_check: The acceleration is 3 m/s^2 to the right. The direction agrees with the larger force and the net-force calculation.
solutions.concept_to_keep: Direction is part of the force model; combine forces before applying the acceleration relation.
